newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish mobile phone use soared in 96.
newsitem.headline: Finnish mobile phone use soared in 96.

text.p: Finnish mobile telephone call sales grew 40 percent last year, leaving them poised to overtake the local fixed-line call market, the government said on Thursday.
"Mobile communications continue to be the fastest-growing area of telecommunications in Finland," the ministry of transport and communications said.
Finland has the highest mobile phone density in the world, with more than 32 handsets per 100 inhabitants.

Mobile phone calls now account for 35 percent of the Finnish market, against 36 percent for local fixed-line calls, the ministry said. The remainder of the market comprises long-distance and international calls plus data transfers.
Net sales of telephone service providers in Finland grew 12.7 percent in 1996 to a total of 12.4 billion markka ($2.4 billion), the ministry said.

State-owned Telecom Finland had the biggest share of the overall market with net sales of 6.2 billion markka. The Finnet group, a consortium of Finnish companies, had sales of 5.7 billion, while Swedish-controlled Telivo Oy and other operators had sales of just 164 million markka.
Finland was among the five countries with the world's lowest mobile phone prices, the ministry said. Finland has the second cheapest local phone call rates in the European Union after Luxembourg.
